book.title: Now, Discover Your Strengths
book.author: Marcus Buckingham and Donald O. Clifton

confidence_note: Question wording, the 20 percent figure with its scope, the meta-analysis numbers and the 'more likely to work in' wording are from Gallup's January 2001 excerpt of the book and from the book's introduction text. The 'eight out of ten feel somewhat miscast' figure has an unclear source in the article and is hedged. Old claims (17 percent, 100 countries, fewer sick days) were wrong and dropped.
facts: The question: 'At work, do you have the opportunity to do what you do best every day?'

Meta-analysis: 198,000 employees, 7,939 business units, 36 companies. Employees who strongly agreed were 50 percent more likely to work in business units with lower turnover, 38 percent more likely in more productive units, 44 percent more likely in units with higher customer satisfaction scores. These are associations, not proven causation.
Business units that raised their number of strongly agreeing employees saw comparable increases in productivity, customer loyalty and retention.

Across a broader database of more than 1.7 million employees in 101 companies in 63 countries, only 20 percent of employees in the large organizations surveyed strongly agreed, meaning they feel their strengths are in play every day.
The longer an employee stays and the higher the person climbs, the less likely they are to strongly agree.
The article says eight out of ten employees feel somewhat miscast in their role, without clearly naming the source of that figure.
As an example, 40 percent would be a doubling of the strongly-agree share; 60 percent, a tripling, is called not too aggressive for the greatest organizations.
tension: The answer is tied to better business units, yet only one in five large-company employees gives the top answer.
opening_idea: One question asked of 198,000 employees and compared with business-unit results.

lessons.idea: Ask the same question of your own week and read the answer as information about task allocation.

reflect_final: Of this week's work, how much room did the thing you do best actually get, by your own sense?

use_cases.situation: You are handing out new responsibilities
use_cases.move: Ask Gallup's question and let the answers shape who takes what.
Ask how much of the week went to what they do best and what you can take off them.

use_cases.situation: You are reviewing your own task list
use_cases.move: Mark the days when you did what you do best.

pocket_idea: Only one in five large-company employees strongly agrees their strengths are in play daily.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Only 20 percent of employees in large organizations strongly agree they get to do what they do best every day.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: One question, 198,000 employees, 50-38-44, and the 20 percent.
